sentences.text:
And Others
 Versus
 Manish @ Munna And 04 Ors., And Others
 Appearance:
Ms. Minu Rajpal - Advocate for the appellants.
Shri Saranjit Singh Chawla, learned counsel for the re  ORDER 1.

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 9/11/2010 passed in Claim Case No.84/2005 challenging the adequacy of compensation.
2. The death of the deceased in the accident is not under challenge.

3. Short facts giving rise to the case are that on 27/6/2005 at around 11.00 AM Bhuraji (hereinafter referred as 'the deceased') with his friend Dinesh on his motorcycle sitting as pillion rider, was going for work from Barwaha to Khandwa.

On Dhangaon and Bethadiya Fata on Indore Khanwa Road near Raghu Dhaba P.S. Dhangaon, District Khandwa, a truck bearing registration No.M.P. 09 U 1039 driven by respondent No.1 came rashly and negligently from Khandwa and dashed against said motorcycle on which the deceased was sitting as a pillion rider, as a result of which the deceased died.

A report was lodged against respondent No.1 at Crime No.139/2005 for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17745 2 MA-1112-2011 offence punishable under Section 304A of IPC.
3.

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the exoneration of the Insurance Company on the ground that the driver was not having license is not proper in view of the fact that for the breach of owner of the vehicle, the claimants should not be made to suffer.
In support of her submissions she has relied on the decision of coordinate Bench of this Court rendered in the case of Cholamandalam MS General Ins. Co. Ltd. V/s. Munni Bai & Ors , 2025 ACJ 821 .

entities.text: Cholamandalam MS General Ins. Co. Ltd. V/s. Munni Bai & Ors , 2025 ACJ 821
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
While referring to the said Chetram And 02 Ors. vs Manish @ Munna And 04 Ors., on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112014176/
1 judgment she has submitted that under similar circumstances this Court has directed for pay and recover.

entities.text: Chetram And 02 Ors. vs Manish @ Munna And 04 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. She further submits that the income of the deceased has not been assessed properly.

By referring to para 14 of the impugned award she submits that the claims tribunal after discarding the evidence of the appellants has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.15000/- per year on notional basis which is very low in view of the fact that the accident has occurred on 27/6/2005.

She by referring to the decision of the Division Bench in the case of Damodar & Anr. V/s. Rajendrasingh & Ors ., 2005 ACJ 474 has contended that in para 7 of the said judgment the Division Bench has considered that now a days earning of Rs.100/- per day by any manual labour is a fact reality.

entities.text: Damodar & Anr. V/s. Rajendrasingh & Ors ., 2005 ACJ 474
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She submits that this order was passed by the Court on 29/7/2004.
She states that in the said case the income of the deceased was taken at Rs.3500/-.
She further submits that in the said case the accident had occurred in the year 1999.

Thus she submits that for an accident occurred six years earlier from the accident of the present case the income was taken at notional basis at Rs.3500/- per month whereas,
in the present case the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17745 3 MA-1112-2011 income has been taken at Rs.15,000/- per annum.

She further submits that the deceased at the time of accident was 24 years of age but the tribunal has applied the multiplier of 16 which should have been 18 in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt.)
and others Vs. Delhi Transport corporation and another , (2009) 6 SCC 121 .

entities.text:
Sarla Verma (Smt.)
and others Vs. Delhi Transport corporation and another , (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She also states that no future prospects have been added in the income of the deceased.

She also submits that for funeral expenses amount of Rs.2000/- has been awarded and for consortium only an amount of Rs.5000/-
has been awarded.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellants be enhanced suitably.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent / Insurance Company supports the findings of the award and by referring to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case of Sardari &
Ors. V/s. Sushil Kumar & Ors. , 2008 ACJ 1307 submits that for breach of policy, the Insurance Company was exonerated from its liability to pay compensation.

entities.text:
Sardari &
Ors. V/s. Sushil Kumar & Ors. , 2008 ACJ 1307
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus there should not be any direction for pay and recover.
As regards the income of the deceased he submits that income at Rs.15,000/- per annum has correctly been taken by the claims tribunal.
Thus he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

As regards contention of the appellants with respect to the liability of the Insurance Company, it is seen from the findings as recorded in para 10 to 12 of the award the license of the driver was not produced by the owner of the vehicle and the Insurance Company has brought witness NAW.2 Vimal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17745 4 MA-1112-2011 Chand Soni who was the Assistant Manager of the Insurance Company who by Exhibits D/03 and D/20 has stated that the driver was resident of Jonpur and the RTO of the Office of Jonpur has provided that no license has been issued to driver Munna @ Manish.
The tribunal has also recorded that the police has also not seized the driving license of the driver during investigation of the accident.
It is thus clear that the findings regarding the breach of policy due to absence of license with the driver of the vehicle are not required to be interfered with.
As regards the submission of the learned counsel for the Chetram And 02 Ors. vs Manish @ Munna And 04 Ors., on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112014176/

entities.text: Chetram And 02 Ors. vs Manish @ Munna And 04 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 appellants that pay and recover should have been directed, it is seen from the observations made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sardari (supra) that in certain situations, the Court while fasting the liability on the owner of the vehicle may direct the Insurance Company to pay to the claimants the awarded amount with liberty to it to recover the same from the owner (para 6).
The coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Cholamandalam (supra) has also upheld the direction of pay and recover.

In view of the above decisions and looking to the fact that the appellants /claimants are poor persons who have suffered because of death of their young son of 24 years of age, it is hereby directed that the Insurance Company shall first pay compensation to the appellants / claimants and then it may recover the same from the owner and/or driver of the vehicle.

8. As regards the adequacy of the compensation, it is indeed considered by the Division Bench of this Court in the case of Damodar (supra) that earning of Rs.100/- per day is a reality and the Court was considering a case of accident in the year 1999.
Thus there is substance in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17745 5 MA-1112-2011 the contention of the appellant that the assessment of income at Rs.15000/- per year is very low.
But looking to the facts of this case, this Court is not inclined to reassess the entire income of the deceased in different heads.

Thus the appellants / claimants are hereby held entitled to receive an additional amount of Rs.1,50,000/-
over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of application.
9. Accordingly, the appeal stands partly allowed and disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
